analysis_steps.goal: Analyze variability and Keplerian rotation of PDS 70c and the inner disc

method.value: Measure flux density and upper limits for PDS 70c across epochs. Test orbital smearing by de-projecting LB19+SB16, rotating by Keplerian motion over 1.75 yr, re-projecting and averaging. Test point-source sensitivity in SB16+IB17 by injecting four 126 uJy fake point sources into residual visibilities. Compare face-on deprojected views of the inner disc across epochs.

evidence.quote: In order to test whether this is an effect of averaging different Keplerian rotation phases, we have de-projected the LB19+SB16 data, transformed the map by Keplerian rotation over a period of 1.75 yr around a 0.9 M_⊙ star, re-projected onto the sky plane and averaged the result with the initial image.

In order to test for synthesis imaging limitations due to the vicinity of the strong and extended emission from the cavity wall, we injected 4 point sources in the residual visibility data, at the expected location of PDS 70c, and at symmetrical positions relative to the disc axes.
The face-on view in Fig. 7b, obtained with the disc orientation given above, shows extended substructure in the inner disc, with a peak at 8σ (labeled ‘Clump 1’in Fig. 7).

claims.result: Standard dirty maps already carry consistent units of Jy per clean beam (sigma = 16.4 uJy/beam in LB19, matching OT predictions), whereas the JvM correction scales residuals by epsilon (down to 1/10), artificially lowering LB19 noise to 6.2 uJy/beam.

claims.hypothesis: A compact mm-wavelength continuum source is present at the location of PDS 70c in the July 2019 (LB19) ALMA observations.
claims.experiment: Non-parametric image synthesis and self-calibration of LB19 and LB19+SB16 datasets using uvmem and OOselfcal, followed by standard image restoration without the JvM correction.
claims.result: Point-like signal coincident with PDS 70c is recovered at 126 +- 16.4 uJy/beam, corresponding to an 8-sigma detection.
claims.finding: The detection of the compact source at PDS 70c in July 2019 is confirmed, though at 8-sigma rather than the higher significance implied by JvM-corrected images.

evidence.quote: In the case of PDS 70, we recover the detection of PDS 70c from the July 2019 data, but only at 8σ.
As summarised in Fig. 4, we confirm the detection of signal coincident with PDS 70c. This is best seen in Fig. 4a, with point-like signal reaching 126 µJy beam^-1, or 8σ.

claims.hypothesis: The mm continuum emission from PDS 70c is constant between Dec. 2017 (IB17) and July 2019 (LB19), and its absence in the concatenated LB19+IB17+SB16 image is merely due to Keplerian orbital smearing.
claims.experiment: Simulated Keplerian rotation averaging over 1.75 yr on the LB19+SB16 image, imaged IB17 and SB16+IB17 directly, and injected four 126 uJy fake point sources into the SB16+IB17 residual visibilities.
claims.result: Keplerian smearing leaves PDS 70c conspicuous; fake 126 uJy sources are recovered within 2-sigma in SB16+IB17, whereas the actual intensity at PDS 70c is -51 uJy/beam in SB16+IB17 and <89 uJy (3-sigma) in IB17.
claims.finding: PDS 70c was absent in Dec. 2017 and brightened by at least 42% +- 13% over the 1.75 yr timespan between IB17 and LB19.

evidence.quote: Fig. 5 shows that, while PDS 70c is somewhat fainter in the average than in the initial image, it is still quite conspicuous.

The non-detection of PDS 70c in IB17 (Fig. 4d) places a 3σ upper limit on its flux density of 89 µJy. Since its flux in LB19 is (126 ± 16.4) µJy beam^-1, if we assign the upper limit flux density to PDS 70c in IB17, then it brightened by 42% ± 13% in the interval of ∼ 1.75 yr between IB17 and LB19.

claims.hypothesis: The inner disc of PDS 70 contains fine, time-variable substructure that rotates and evolves between epochs.
claims.experiment: Deprojected face-on comparison of the restored LB19+SB16 image and the super-resolved SB16+IB17 uvmem model image.
claims.result: An 8-sigma peak (Clump 1) offset by ~0''.03-0''.04 from the ring center rotates by ~70 deg in azimuth between IB17 and LB19 (consistent with Keplerian rotation at 3.4-4.5 au), while a second peak (Clump 2 at ~0''.08 in IB17) cannot be explained by circular Keplerian rotation alone.
claims.finding: The inner disc of PDS 70 is structured and variable, exhibiting both Keplerian rotation of Clump 1 and intrinsic morphological changes.

evidence.quote: We also pick up fine structure in the inner disc, such that its peak is offset by ∼ 0''.04 from the disc centre. The inner disc is variable too, which we tentatively ascribe to Keplerian rotation as well as intrinsic morphological changes.
We find Clump 1 offset by ∼ 70 deg in azimuth relative to SB16+LB19, as expected for Keplerian rotation if the centre of mass coincides with the ring center.

why_this_data.value: The direct detection of a CPD around PDS 70c in deep long-baseline ALMA observations is a momentous achievement in planetary sciences, motivating a reanalysis of the available multi-epoch ALMA datasets with careful attention to uncertainties.

evidence.quote: The direct detection of a CPD, thanks to deep ALMA observations, is a momentous achievement in planetary sciences, whose relevance motivates us to revisit these data with alternative synthesis imaging tools.

why_this_method.value: Non-parametric image synthesis with uvmem provides an alternative to CLEAN, and uv-plane alignment via VisAlign restricts free parameters to a single position shift and flux scale factor without requiring a bright source model like joint self-calibration.

evidence.quote: Here we perform nonparametric image synthesis using the uvmem package (Casassus et al. 2006; Cárcamo et al. 2018) as an alternative to the more commonly used clean algorithm

The result of our procedure is similar to that of joint self-calibration (described in Sec. 3.1), but it restricts the number of unknowns to only a single position shift and a flux scale factor, while self-calibration adjusts time-series for the antenna gains.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Entropy regularization in uvmem was tested, yielding a lower flux density ratio of 0.77 +- 0.004, but was rejected in favor of pure chi^2 optimization with image positivity because entropy regularization produced stronger synthesis imaging artifacts.

evidence.quote: Using entropy regularization resulted in a lower flux density ratio of 0.77 ± 0.004 (but with stronger synthesis imaging artifacts, which is why we use the pure χ^2 versions).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Time-variability of the bulk outer disc flux density as the cause of the ~20% flux scale difference between SB16 and IB17/LB19 was rejected as unlikely because IB17 and LB19 have consistent flux scales over a similar time interval.

evidence.quote: The alternative, that the flux of the disc itself is time-variable, is unlikely since the flux scales between IB17 and LB19 are consistent, while the time separations between IB17 and SB16, and between LB19 and IB17, are similar.

limitations_admitted.value: The LB19 flux density is biased upwards in the pure chi^2 uvmem reconstructions due to positive-definite noise in the model images.

evidence.quote: The LB19 flux density is biased upwards in our pure χ^2 reconstructions, because of the positive-definite noise in the model images.

limitations_admitted.value: The statistical properties and uncertainties of the unconvolved uvmem model image are not well constrained, making the comparison of the SB16+IB17 model image with the restored SB16+LB19 image for the inner disc tentative.

evidence.quote: Since the statistical properties of the model image are not well constrained, the comparison is tentative.

evidence.loc: A1 Motivation for image restoration, and for a reconsideration of the JvM correction
evidence.quote: However, the model images by themselves usually lack noise estimates. This is because the inverse problem in image synthesis, i.e. the production of a model image from sparse Fourier data, is intrinsically ill-posed.

referee_caveats_inferred: The comparison of inner disc substructure across epochs relies on comparing an unconvolved super-resolved uvmem model image (SB16+IB17) against a convolved restored image (SB16+LB19), which have different effective PSF responses and noise statistics.
The initial continuum visibility extraction and spectral window flagging are not explicitly detailed and rely entirely on the procedures of Benisty et al. (2021).
